prep.summary: You must address the transition from rigid Guidewire tasks—where the team slashed activities by 38%—to a dynamic notification model centering on Capgemini's "Next Best Action" concept. Business leadership demands rapid 90-day progress on timeline alerts and status updates—bypassing the slow Q1 2027 target—but faces resistance from IT Leadership—specifically Dan Griffiths—who rejected funding for 32 extra resource positions. Your upcoming design sessions with Sarah Hudson must bridge this gap—focusing on reducing adjuster "snowblindness" through intelligent prioritization without adding technical complexity.
tasks: Connect with Director Rolando to finalize the pending action items from the July 22nd UX sync.
Align with Sarah Hudson on the 90-day quick-win designs—prioritizing the pairing of timeline quality and status updates.
Resolve the staffing discrepancy with Dan Griffiths—securing internal IT resources to offset the rejected Capgemini headcount.
Define the parameters of the "Next Best Action" framework—replacing flat Guidewire alerts with dynamic, context-aware priorities.
prep.title: Future of Adjuster Alerting/ Notification Design
